children: Top East African retail banks have been named among the world’s top-performing lenders, reflecting their sustained profit trends and raising the profile of the region’s banking sector among foreign investors and depositors seeking strong, stable institutions.
Regional lenders, mainly from Kenya, Tanzania, and the DR Congo, have been included in Forbes’ list of the world’s 500 best-performing banks.

Kenya’s Co-operative Bank, KCB Group, Equity Group and Stanbic Holdings all feature in Forbes’ inaugural list of the world’s top-performing banks. Also on the list are NMB and CRDB banks from Tanzania, and RawBank from the DRC.

Forbes evaluated 500 banks across 89 countries, examining their profitability, strength, stability and efficiency in funding mega trade and infrastructure projects, as well as safeguarding the interests of shareholders and depositors.

In its inaugural World’s Top Performing Banks 2026 ranking published on September 10, Forbes, in partnership with market research firm Statista, named seven East African lenders among the world’s elite financial institutions, reflecting their sustained earnings and asset growth.

This global recognition highlights the robust operational strength and growing influence of East Africa’s banking sector within the international financial ecosystem. Eligible banks were classified into six tiers based on their total assets, enabling the analysis to compare financial institutions within their respective peer group sizes.

These included Tier 1 banks, which are mainly global banks with more than $500 billion in total assets, Tier 2 (large banks) with $100 billion to $500 billion in total assets and Tier 3 (upper mid-size banks) with $50 billion to $100 billion worth of assets. Tier 4 (mid-size banks) were classified as those holding $20 billion to $50 billion in assets , Tier 5 (lower mid-size banks) with $10 billion to $20 billion in assets and Tier 6 (small banks) with $3 billion to $10 billion in assets.

The lenders which met these criteria were then evaluated across four main performance matrices with profitability accounting for the bulk of the scores, at 30 per cent, followed by capital and funding resilience (25 per cent), asset quality and efficiency (25 per cent) and growth and earnings quality (20 per cent). According to the ranking Equity and KCB secured positions 71 and 79 globally respectively among the tier 5 banks (lower mid-size banks) which hold $10 billion to $20 billion worth of assetsTanzania’s NMB and CRDB banks secured the number nine and 41 spots respectively in among the Tier 6 (small) banks which groups global institutions holding between $3 billion and $10 billion in assets Co-op Bank secured the 120th spot in Tier 6 banks, followed by Stanbic bank Holdings at position 138 and DRC’s RawBank at position 145.

Zimbabwe also had three banks in the global list of 500 top performing lenders, with its lenders CBZ and FBC Holdings securing position one and 25 respectively in the Tier 2 (large banks) with $100 billion to $500 billion in total assets.

NMBZ Holdings (Zimbabwe) took position 10 in the Tier 3 (upper mid-size banks) with $50 billion to $100 billion worth of assets. A review of the half-year financial performances of some of the top East African banks on the global list of the best performing lenders shows a surge in profitability and asset bases highlighting their financial strength.

Kenya’s Co-op bank, which has operations in South Sudan, posted a 28 per cent growth in net profit to Ksh18.02 billion($139.68 million) in the first half of the year ended June 30 2026 driven by increased interest and non-interest income. The group’s net earnings grew from Ksh14.08 billion ($109.14 million) posted in a similar period last year, with its non-performing loans (NPLs) ratio improving to 13.9 per cent from 17.2 per cent.
Its asset base grew to Ksh869.47 billion ($6.74 billion) from Ksh811.91 billion ($6.29 million), while deposits increased by 13.4 percent to Ksh621.27 billion ($4.81 million).

Equity Group Holdings posted a record 31.5 per cent year-on-year surge in net profit to Ksh43.57 billion($337.75 million) for the first half of 2026, from Ksh33.3 billion($258.13 million) in the same period last year driven by an expanding asset base which grew by 20 per cent to Sh2.16 trillion and substantial contributions from its cross-border regional subsidiaries.

KCB group reported a 14.2 per cent growth in net profit to Ksh36 billion($279.06 million) in the first half of the year ended June 2026 from Ksh31.5 billion($244.18 million) posted in the same period last year, driven largely cheaper cost of funds and lower loan provisioning following improved quality of its loan book. Stanbic Holdings recorded a one percent growth in net profit to Ksh6.6 billion ($51.16 million) for the six months ended June 2026 from Ksh6.54 billion ($50.69 million) in the same period last yearNMB banks half-year net profit grew to Tsh212.41 billion ($80.39 million) from Tsh173.05 billion ($65.49 million) in the same period last year, with asset base growing to Tsh18.43 trillion ($6.97 billion) from Tsh17.92 trillion ($6.78 billion).

CRDB recorded a 20.3 per cent surge in its half- year net profit to Tsh416.85 billion ($157.76m) from Tsh346.45 billion ($131.11m), while total assets grew by 33.9 percent to Tsh26.39 trillion ($9.98 billion) from Tsh19.7 trillion ($7.45 billion) in the same period last year.
